name: Artist Spotlight
howWeMakeIt: Three to five key works chosen
One quote from the artist
Chain of Influence link to an archive artist, if there is one
Artist approval
Assets cleared

name: From the Vault
description: Resurface an important or overlooked piece of archive material and give it a reason to exist today. The cheapest post we make and the easiest to make badly.
jobRationale: Explore. Pushes people from one post into the archive itself.
formatSpec: 6–7 frames, 4:5. F1 the artwork uncropped. F2–F5 detail crops. F6 the context, under 60 words. F7 archive CTA.
effort: Low. About 3 hours, one person, no shoot.
howWeMakeIt: Check the run log: nothing that has run on the account in the last 24 months
Clear it with Colburn first, before writing. Vault material is the highest-risk category we publish
Find the reason it matters now: an anniversary, a theme link or a modern echo. No reason, no post
Clean the scan: a levels and dust pass before it goes near a frame
Write the claim: sixty words, one thing the reader should believe by the end
watchOut: “Old thing, isn’t it great” is not a post. If you can’t finish the sentence “this matters because…”, it’s a repost, not a Vault.

name: Cover Story
description: The story behind one cover: how it was made, what got rejected, and where it ended up.
jobRationale: Reach + Explore. Covers are our most recognisable asset, and this is the format that gets shared off-platform.
formatSpec: 5–7 frames, 4:5. F1 the cover full-bleed. F2 the detail people miss. F3–F4 roughs or rejected versions. F5 where it went. F6 CTA.
effort: Low to medium. About 4 hours, one person, longer if chasing roughs.
howWeMakeIt: Asset kit received: Q&A, process photos, roughs, timelapse, portrait
Roughs or rejected versions chosen for F3–F4. No roughs means it isn’t a Cover Story
Credits and details checked against the final printed cover
At least one detail frame: something the reader would miss on a first look
Artist page on the website
Cut for paid: the full-bleed cover is our best-performing static ad format. Always supply it, if the cover passes ad policy
watchOut: No roughs, no controversy, no first appearance? Then it’s a From the Vault. Don’t stretch the format to fit a cover you happen to like.

name: Essential Reading
description: A curated reading list built around one theme, artist or character. Our highest-saving format and the most reliable driver of archive and membership clicks.
jobRationale: Explore + Act. The clearest route from a scroll to a subscription. Always ends on the archive.
formatSpec: 6–8 frames, 4:5. F1 theme title over the strongest artwork. F2–F6 one story each: title, creators, volume and issue, one line on why. F7 CTA.

frames.label: F1
frames.instruction: theme title over the strongest artwork

frames.label: F2–F6
frames.instruction: one story each: title, creators, volume and issue, one line on why

effort: Low. About 4 hours, one person, no shoot.
howWeMakeIt: Pick a theme narrow enough to argue with. “Greatest heroines” works, “great stories” doesn’t
Cap it at five. Four is better
Number every entry: volume and issue on every frame
Check every story is actually readable in the archive. If it isn’t there yet, it doesn’t go on the list
Order it: strongest image first, strongest argument last
watchOut: This format converts. Never publish it without a working archive or membership link. A saved list with a dead CTA is a wasted post.

name: Issue Guide
description: A page-by-page breakdown of a single issue: the artists, the stories, the one moment worth the cover price. Works for new releases and archive issues.
jobRationale: Explore + Act. On a new release it drives the shop. On an archive issue it drives membership.
formatSpec: 7–9 frames, 4:5. F1 cover + issue number and date. F2 the cover artist. F3–F6 one story each with page range. F7 the standout moment, page and panel. F8 CTA.

frames.label: F3–F6
frames.instruction: one story each with page range

frames.label: F7
frames.instruction: the standout moment, page and panel

effort: Medium. About 5 hours, one person, needs the physical issue.
howWeMakeIt: Get the issue in your hands, or a full scan. Contents pages are unreliable and often omit contributors
Log every story: title, creators, page range. Build the log before you write a word
Verify credits against the printed page, not a database or a wiki
Pick one standout moment and give it a page and panel number
Route the CTA: a new release goes to the shop (Commerce confirms five weeks out), an archive issue goes to membership
watchOut: Credits are the thing the comments will catch. If a credit can’t be verified against the printed page, leave the name off rather than guess.

name: Studio Visit
description: Behind the scenes in one artist’s workspace: the room, the tools, the piece currently on the desk. The room is the story.
jobRationale: Explore. Our most requested format, and the warmest introduction we have to a future affiliate partner.
formatSpec: 3–5 minutes, 16:9 for YouTube, with vertical cutdowns. Interview plus B-roll, natural light where possible.
effort: Medium. Two days: half-day shoot, one day edit, half-day cutdowns.
howWeMakeIt: Recce by video call first: ask them to walk the room on their phone. It’s a shot list and a lighting check in one
Shoot B-roll before the interview, so you get the room before anyone has moved through it
Six hero details minimum: the tools, the wall, the reference pile, the mess
Interview at the desk, not against a wall. Let the room stay in frame
Cut three verticals, each built around a single object, for Reels and TikTok
watchOut: Don’t let them tidy. The clutter is the content. If they’ve cleaned for you, ask what they moved and put it back.

name: Behind the Drop
description: The making of the capsule, from first sample to launch day. Justifies the price before anyone has seen the price.
jobRationale: Act. Runs in the two weeks before the drop and does the selling the product page can’t.
formatSpec: 60–90 seconds, 9:16 primary. Process footage, rejected samples, the maker talking. Cut fast.
effort: Medium. Filmed across the development window, two-day edit.
howWeMakeIt: Start filming at sample one. If you start late there is nothing to show and it can’t be recovered
Keep every rejected sample. Photograph and label each one as it fails
One person on camera: the designer or the maker, not a committee
Show a number: sample rounds, stitch count, months in development
Lock the edit five weeks out, so Commerce can confirm the drop date against it
watchOut: This only works if you filmed early. It can’t be reconstructed at launch, and staged process footage reads as fake immediately.

name: Heavily Influenced
description: An artist walks through the films, comics, music and creators that formed them. A lineage interview that places Heavy Metal inside a wider culture.
jobRationale: Explore. Positions the brand as part of a culture rather than the centre of one, and travels through the influences’ audiences too.
formatSpec: 6–10 minutes, 16:9 with clips, plus a Spotify audio cut. Four to six influences, one segment each, same structure throughout.
effort: High. Four weeks lead, one shoot day, week-long edit plus clearance.
howWeMakeIt: Get the influence list at booking. The whole shoot is built around it. No list, no date
Send the influence list to Colburn the day it’s booked. Film stills, album art and third-party comics all need clearing before the shoot
One segment per influence, same structure. The repetition is the format
Where a work can’t be cleared, shoot them describing it instead
Deliver the audio cut for Spotify
watchOut: Rights on other people’s material, not ours, is what stalls this format.

name: Collection Lookbook
description: The definitive visual record of the capsule: campaign imagery, styling and every key piece. The reference asset the whole drop borrows from.
jobRationale: Act. Feeds the shop, the ads, wholesale and press for the entire life of the collection.
formatSpec: Stills series, 4:5 primary with 16:9 crops. 12–20 images: campaign, on-figure, flat lay. Optional fashion film.
effort: High. Pre-production week, 1–2 shoot days, week-long retouch.
howWeMakeIt: Lock the shot list against the line sheet: every product on-figure and flat
Cast and style to the brand, not the season. The archive is the mood board
Shoot flats the same day, same light
Retouch to a written standard, so drops still match each other a year later
Deliver a split pack: social crops, shop imagery, ad crops, press resolution
watchOut: Everything else borrows from this shoot. Under-shooting it costs far more later than the extra half-day costs now.
